definition: The dual-attitude model proposes that people can hold two attitudes about the same subject at once: a more deliberate, openly reported attitude and a more automatic, less conscious attitude. In this study, it is used to explain how psychotherapists could report especially positive views about mental illness while still showing negative implicit bias that may be shaped by broader social influences and be harder to change.
